strategicCamps.description: A powerful but strategically overextended United States operating largely without its former transatlantic coalition.
A coalition fighting both the United States in the North Atlantic and Russia in Europe, with significant aggregate capacity but incomplete integration and disrupted supply chains.
States with different goals that begin by avoiding conflict with each other and may coordinate opportunistically without acting as a unified alliance.

diplomaticPostures.notes: Scenario premise: relations are unusually cordial despite incompatible interests elsewhere. The relationship can deteriorate or deepen through simulation.
Scenario premise: relations are unusually cordial but do not imply alliance obligations.
They begin by avoiding conflict with each other and can trade or coordinate, but have no automatic shared-war obligation.
High strategic tension, but no automatic shooting war at scenario start.

american-power: loss or uncertainty of traditional European basing and logistics
simultaneous war with Iran and the European defence coalition
european-defence-coalition: incomplete transition away from Russian fossil-fuel dependence
incomplete transition away from United States military imports
fragmented procurement, stockpiles and mobilisation across members
eurasian-accommodation: exposure to sanctions, maritime interdiction and trade-route disruption

notes: This file encodes the fictional scenario premise, not assertions about real-world events.
Territory and sea selectors will be resolved when the dedicated modern strategic map is authored.
The simulation should determine future alliances, neutrality, mediation, escalation and settlement from game systems rather than event scripting.
Strategic camps are descriptive starting geometries, not permanent teams. Members may diverge if simulation incentives and domestic politics push them apart.
